sections.text: ONE OR MORE CLUSTERS OF STORMS WILL PROBABLY BE ONGOING AT 12Z...NEAR A LOWER/MID TROPOSPHERIC BAROCLINIC ZONE FROM PARTS OF NORTHEAST KANSAS/SOUTHEAST NEBRASKA THROUGH SOUTHERN IOWA/NORTHERN MISSOURI INTO PARTS OF NORTHWEST ILLINOIS. sections.title: KS/OK INTO THE OH VALLEY
sections.text: SURFACE LOW OVER THE NRN TX OR OK PNHDL AS OF 19Z IS FORECAST TO DEVELOP SLOWLY EWD THROUGH THE REMAINDER OF THE AFTERNOON BEFORE FORMING MORE RAPIDLY NEWD ALONG QUASI-STATIONARY BOUNDARY INTO NERN MO BY SUNDAY MORNING. LATEST GPS PW DATA INDICATE THAT RICHER MOISTURE HAS BEEN DISPLACED TO THE E OF DRYLINE AND WRN EXTENSION OF SYNOPTIC FRONTAL BOUNDARY DUE TO PRONOUNCED SWLY FLOW ABOVE THE SURFACE PER VWP/PROFILER OBSERVATIONS. HOWEVER...MASS RESPONSE TO APPROACHING UPPER LEVEL TROUGH WILL RESULT IN THE REFORMATION OF A SLY LLJ OVER KS AND OK BY THIS EVENING WHICH SHOULD SUPPORT THE NWD/NWWD ADVECTION OF RICHER MOISTURE TOWARD KS PORTION OF FRONTAL ZONE. IN THE NEAR TERM...STRONGER DIABATIC HEATING ALONG WRN FRINGE OF MID/HIGH CLOUD SHIELD HAS SUPPORTED THE DEVELOPMENT OF A STEEP LAPSE RATE ENVIRONMENT ALONG SURFACE FRONT FROM THE TX/OK PNHDLS NEWD INTO CNTRL KS. THESE LAPSE RATES IN CONJUNCTION WITH THE MODEST MOISTURE ARE EXPECTED TO CONTRIBUTE TO A MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIR MASS LATER THIS AFTERNOON WITH MLCAPE APPROACHING 1000-1500 J/KG. 12Z RUNS OF THE NAM AND HIGHER RESOLUTION NMM DATA SETS SUGGEST SURFACE-BASED STORMS ARE POSSIBLE WITHIN THIS CORRIDOR PRIOR TO 00Z.
